nodes.name: Anodization of Mo foil
nodes.procedure: A piece of Mo foil (1×2 cm) was washed with hydrochloric acid, acetone, deionized water (DI-water) and absolute ethyl alcohol, respectively. Then, the electrochemical oxidation was carried out and controlled in the PBS solution at 0.5 V for 10 s, 100 s and 300 s using Mo foil, Pt foil and saturated calomel electrode (SCE) as work electrode. The anodized Mo foil was named MoO_x-t (t is the oxidation time).

nodes.name: Chemical oxidation of Mo foil
nodes.procedure: The MoO2 was synthesized by placing the cleaned Mo foil in a stainless steel autoclave containing 10 mL DI-water and 0.1 mL H2O2 at 60°C for 12 h.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis Mo-Co/MoOx
nodes.procedure: Typically, 0.29 g CoCl2·6H2O, 0.92 g NH4Cl and 0.37 g urea were dissolved in 20 mL DI-water and stirred for 10 min. Then the well-mixed solution and MoO_x were put into a Teflon-lined stainless steel autoclave at 120°C for 6 h. After cooling to room temperature, the Mo foil grown with Co precursor was washed with ethanol and DI-water, respectively, and then vacuum-dried for preservation. The Mo-Co/MoO2 was prepared using the same method except for MoO2 as the substrate.

nodes.name: Phosphorization of Mo-Co precursors
nodes.procedure: The quartz boat loaded as-prepared Mo-Co/MoO_x or Mo-Co/MoO_2 was placed downstream of the tube furnace and the quartz boat with 0.5 g NaH2PO2 at upstream. Then the tube furnace was programmed to 300°C with a heating rate of 2°C min^-1 under Ar atmosphere. The resulting samples were denoted as Mo-CoP/MoO_x·t (t is the oxidation time).

nodes.name: Fluoroaniline coating
nodes.procedure: The above Mo-CoP/MoO_x was immersed in a fluoroaniline solution of 15 mL containing 0.022 g fluoroaniline for 30 s. Then the obtained sample was rinsed several times with DI-water to remove excess fluoroaniline and named F-Mo-CoP/MoOx.

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo-CoP/MoO_x mainly comprises CoP (011, 200, 111, 112, 202, 301, 203 planes) and CoP2 (020, 210, 121, -131, -132, 320 planes) phases with diffraction peaks slightly shifted to smaller angles confirming Mo doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 2a shows that the final Mo-CoP/MoO_x, CoP powder and CoP/MF ... can be assigned to the (011), (200), (111), (112), (202), (301) and (203) crystal planes of CoP ... peaks located at 33.5°, 39.2°, 44.1°, 53.4°, 59.3° and 65.1° can be indexed to the (020), (210), (121), (-131), (-132) and (320) crystal face of CoP2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo-CoP/MoO_x manifests vertical robust nanoneedle structure with slight twists and rougher surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After phosphorization, the vertical robust Mo-CoP/MoO_x manifests a similar acicular structure to pristine Co nanoarrays except for slight twists and rougher surface (Fig. 2b, c).

properties.description: High-magnification SEM image showing dense, brush-like nanostructure with fibrous morphology

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows Mo-CoP/MoO_x with CoP (011) d=0.281 nm and (111) d=0.225 nm lattices, clear interface with Mo (110) plane, lattice dislocations due to Mo; F-Mo-CoP/MoO_x shows core-shell structure with ~10 nm amorphous shell.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 2e shows ... nanoneedle-like CoP structure ... HRTEM (Fig. 2f), which displays two clear CoP crystal lattices of (011) and (111) phases with the d-spacings of 0.281 and 0.225 nm ... no MoP lattices are discerned, and the discernible lattice dislocations ... Further coated by polyfluoroaniline layer ... F-Mo-CoP/MoO_x shows a distinct core-shell structure comprised of an amorphous shell with a thickness of ~10 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM-EDX mapping confirms uniform distribution of Mo, Co, P in Mo-CoP/MoO_x nanoneedles with atomic ratio Co:P:Mo = 38:61:1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 2e shows the scanning transmission electron microscope (STEM)-energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX), demonstrating the nanoneedle-like CoP structure and uniformly dispersed Mo, Co and P elements with the atomic ratio of Co:P:Mo around 38:61:1 (Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: Clear interface between CoP (011)/(111) planes and Mo (110) plane observed in Mo-CoP/MoO_x with lattice dislocations due to Mo introduction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: More information is provided by HRTEM (Fig. 2f), which displays two clear CoP crystal lattices of (011) and (111) phases with the d-spacings of 0.281 and 0.225 nm ... It is worth mentioning that no MoP lattices are discerned, and the discernible lattice dislocations and defects are presumably due to the introduction of the relatively large-radius Mo.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED confirms CoP phases in Mo-CoP/MoO_x.
nodes.evidence_snippet: that can be manifested by the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) image in Fig. 2g.

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo-CoP/MoO_x shows Co 2p peaks at 778.57 eV (Co-P), 793.47 eV (Co-P), positive shift ~0.3 eV vs Mo-Co/MoO_x indicating strong Co-P interaction, negative shift vs pure CoP confirming Mo doping effect; Mo 3d shows Mo3+, Mo4+, Mo5+; P 2p peaks negatively shifted ~0.39 eV vs pure CoP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co 2p_{1/2} and Co 2p_{3/2} can be separated into two new typical peaks at 778.57 and 793.47 eV, respectively, which are indexed to Co-P species ... In addition, Co 2p peaks of Mo-CoP/MoO_x show a positive shift of ~0.3 eV ... the Mo 3d spectra in Mo-CoP/MoO_x sample (Fig. 3b) can only be deconvoluted into three types Mo (Mo^{3+}, Mo^{4+} and Mo^{5+}) ... the binding energies of P 2p_{1/2} and P 2p_{3/2} are negatively shifted (~0.39 eV) compared with pure CoP powder.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge XANES of Mo-CoP/MoO_x shifts to lower energy compared to CoP, indicating decreased oxidation of Co.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 3c shows the detected X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) of CoP and Mo-CoP/MoO_x, and it can be observed that the XANES edge of Mo-CoP/MoO_x shifts to lower energy compared to pure CoP.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT k^3-weighted EXAFS shows primary peak at 1.8 Å for Co-P bond; fitting confirms Co-P and Co-Co bonds, no Mo-P bond; lower peak intensity indicates falling coordination number after Mo doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For the Fourier-transformed (FT) k^3-weighted extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) in Fig. 3d, the primary peak around 1.8 Å can be attributed to the Co—P bond ... Fig. S7 and Table S4 show the existence of Co—P and Co—Co bond, while no Mo-P can be assigned ... The lower peak intensity of Mo-CoP/MoO_x also suggests the falling coordination number of Co and distorted crystal structure after Mo incorporation.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS Nyquist plots show maximum conductivity for Mo-CoP/MoO_x-100.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Nyquist plots fitted by an equivalent circuit model in the inset of Fig. 4d illustrate the maximum conductivity of Mo-CoP/MoO_x-100.

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance C_dl = 35.8 mF cm^{-2} for Mo-CoP/MoO_x-100 (vs 28.8 mF cm^{-2} for Mo-Co/MoO_x-100, 10.9 mF cm^{-2} for CoP/MF).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig.4e shows no significant difference in C_dl value between Mo-Co/MoO_x-100 28.8 mF cm^{-2} and Mo-CoP/MoO_x-100 (35.8 mF cm^{-2}). However, the CoP/MF shows much lower ECSA with C_dl of 10.9 mF cm^{-2}.

nodes.characterization_summary: MoO_x shows metallic Mo (200) 58.64°, (211) 73.60° and MoO3 (020) 23.83° peaks, absence of Mo (110) peak confirms abundant active molybdenum.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As Fig. S2a shows, the two characteristic peaks at 58.64° and 73.60° can be well assigned to the (200) and (211) crystal planes of metallic Mo (JCPDS No: 42-1120), and the peak at 23.83° matches well with the (020) plane of MoO3 (JCPDS No: 80-0347), which, together with the absence of Mo (110) peak, implies the formation of abundant active molybdenum.
